made: node docs/proyecto/pixel/pedido-sheet-make.js, from pedido-set.html (window.PEDIDO.E, E.SEATS and E.PANELS) and the design of El pedido (the orchestrator's p8-spec, general rules and section pedido). A new scene: no old scene, no remap.

rules.project: pp-engine.js project(x, y, z) with S 26 and this origin: sx = OX + (x - y) / R2 * S, sy = OY + ((x + y) / R2 * .5 - z * COS) * S, depth d = (x + y) / R2 * COS + z * .5 (R2 = sqrt 2, COS = sqrt 3 / 2); OX = W / 2 + originX = 120, OY = H / 2 + originY = 66. A box is the screen bounding box of its projected corners [floor(min x), floor(min y), ceil(max x) - floor(min x), ceil(max y) - floor(min y)]. screen is the projection rounded to whole pixels
rules.uv: the set is laid out square to the picture: a spot is given in (u, v, z), u across the picture (to the right), v down it (towards the camera), the back wall at v 0; plaza-base.js PZ.xy(u, v) = ((u + v) / R2, (v - u) / R2) gives the world x, y (world is that). On the picture sx = OX + u * S = 120 + 26 u, and sy = OY + (v / 2 - z * COS) * S = 66 + 13 v - 22.5 z; the picture holds u from -4.62 to 4.62. The family's chairs are E.SEATS (FD.setTable's places): silla1 (-1.225, 4.14), silla2 (-0.275, 4.14), silla3 (0.675, 4.14), silla4 (1.625, 4.14)
rules.spot: a spot is a world point of the feet (z 0: the floor; z 0.44: a chair's top; z 0.74: the table's top; z 1: the hatch's shelf) and, drawn there, a character stands with its feet (the lowest row the sprite draws, outline included) resting on the screen row sy, i.e. the sprite's bottom edge on sy, and its middle column on the column sx (rules.anchor). A small thing has a box (the spot's box): a plate, a drink, the tall glass and the small plate have their bottom middle on the spot (the box [sx - floor(w / 2), sy - h, w, h]); the plantains hang with their top middle on the hook's point (the box [sx - 7, sy, 14, 18]); a picture on a panel is centred on the panel's middle (the box [sx - 7, sy - 6, 14, 12]; a panel is about 13 x 10 px, so a picture overlaps its frame by a pixel or two). scale is the frog's: 1 everywhere
rules.anchor: the column of the sprite that is on sx; its feet (its lowest drawn row, outline included) rest on row sy - 1, so its bottom edge is on sy. mkPersona (48 wide): column 24 (KIT.PX), 53 rows drawn standing for a grown-up (a 56-row canvas whose lowest row is empty); the frog mkCoqui(1) (32 x 27): column 16, drawn rows 1 to 24 (row 25 of the canvas is on sy); abuela sitting mkAbuelaS (52 x 50): column 17 (her middle) and row 36 (her lap) on (sx, sy), the spot being the chair; a grown-up sitting (mkPersona with sent = 1): column 24 and the lap row, the bottom of the hips: row 16 + 2 t + 3 (t 11 a grown-up: 41; t 7 a child: 33) on (sx, sy); the cat (El camino's mkGato sitting, 26 x 20): column 12 and its bottom edge; a small thing: see spot. Nobody is drawn turned: whoever sits at the table or stands behind the wall faces us
rules.view: one window, wide, zoom 1: the 196 x 216 window over the 240 x 216 picture, x0 = its left edge (22 centres it). Never a fraction
rules.depth: a spot's depth is the engine's d of its world point; front.plane turns it into the depth of each row of a character
rules.cocinero: the cocinero's spot hueco is behind the wall (v -.4, the kitchen's back wall is v -1.5): the wall, the shelf and the table hide him below the hatch's sill, and the hatch's hole (u -0.85 to 2.95, z 1 to 2.62) shows him from the chest up

front.how: no list. A character is hidden by every set pixel that is nearer the camera than the character's feet (depth test against the baked depth, with the feet's depth plus 0.3): the table hides the lap and legs of whoever sits behind it, the wall and the shelf hide the cocinero below the hatch's sill, the next table hides its guests from the waist down.
front.plane: for the character's pixel on picture row r (r = 0 at the top): depth(r) = d + (sy - (r + .5)) * tan(30 deg) / S, where d is the spot's depth and sy its screen row; the pixel is hidden where bakedZ[r * 240 + x] > depth(r) + bias (bakedZ: window.DEPTH.z of the set page). The same rule as El cruce's sheet: the upright plane through the feet (a picture on a panel is the plane through its middle, on the wall)
front.sprites: between two sprites the nearer pixel wins: the same depth(r), no bias; two planes within 0.001 are a tie and the later layer is drawn

shadows.at: castShadow(x, y, 0, radius) at the world x, y of the spot, for a character standing on the floor (z 0). The spec gives no radius: these are El cruce's (frog .45, grown-ups .35, children .28) and .2 for the cat (open point)
